answer: Two (2) VPN tunnels between a virtual private gateway or transit gateway on the AWS side and a customer gateway device in your data center.

answer: An RCP is an AWS Organizations policy that centrally sets the maximum available permissions for AWS resources in the organization (preventative controls on resources). Typical use: restrict access to your resources so that only identities that belong to your organization can access them, or set the conditions under which external identities can access them.
quote: RCP is an AWS Organizations policy that you can use to define and enforce preventative controls on AWS resources in your organization. Using RCPs, you can centrally set the maximum available permissions to your AWS resources as you scale your workloads on AWS. For example, an RCP can help restrict access to your resources so that they can only be accessed by identities that belong to your organization, or specifying the conditions under which identities external to your organization can access your resources.
reason: Re-derived from the AWS Organizations FAQ answer to 'What is a resource control policy (RCP)?'.

answer: A role trust policy is a required resource-based JSON policy attached to an IAM role; its Principal element defines the principals (users, roles, accounts, services) that you trust to assume the role.

answer: Yes. Through an internet gateway to a public AWS service endpoint in the same Region there are no data transfer charges; through a NAT gateway there is a per-GB data processing charge for data that passes through the gateway.
quote: If the internet gateway is used to access the public endpoint of the AWS services in the same Region (Figure 1 – Pattern 1), there are no data transfer charges. If a NAT gateway is used to access the same services (Figure 1 – Pattern 2), there is a data processing charge (per gigabyte (GB)) for data that passes through the gateway.
reason: Re-derived from the AWS Architecture Blog post on data transfer costs; the VPC pricing page example ($0.045 per GB NAT processing, S3 same Region) agrees.

answer: Customer-managed prefix lists are sets of IP address ranges that you define and manage, and you can share them with other AWS accounts. AWS-managed prefix lists are sets of IP address ranges for AWS services; you cannot create, modify, share, or delete them.

answer: A beta exam is used by AWS Certification to validate the performance of exam questions before they are used on standard versions. It differs from the standard exam: it contains more total questions and more scored questions, is available for a limited period (generally 1 to 3 months), is offered at a discount, and can be taken only once.
quote: A beta exam contains more total questions and more scored questions than the standard version of the same exam.
reason: Re-derived from the Before Testing policy page, section 'Beta exams'; the Certification FAQ gives the same definition.

answer: Resources in the other Availability Zones lose internet access. For resiliency, create one NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and route each zone's resources to the NAT gateway in the same zone.
quote: If you have resources in multiple Availability Zones and they share one NAT gateway, and if the NAT gateway's Availability Zone is down, resources in the other Availability Zones lose internet access.

answer: An RCP limits permissions on resources in member accounts, so it can affect any identity that accesses them, including the AWS account root user, whether or not the identity belongs to your organization. Choose an RCP over an SCP when you want to restrict access to your resources (for example by identities external to your organization); an SCP only limits the principals (users and roles) in your own accounts.
quote: The RCP limits permissions for resources in member accounts and can impact the effective permissions for identities, including the AWS account root user, regardless of whether they belong to your organization.
reason: Re-derived from the IAM policy types page, section 'AWS Organizations resource control policies (RCPs)'; the SCP section of the same page says SCPs set maximum permissions for IAM users and roles within the organization.

answer: When the instance and the NAT gateway are in different Availability Zones; traffic between them in the same Availability Zone over private IP addresses has no data transfer charge.
quote: There was also no charge for the data transfer between the NAT gateway and the EC2 instance since the traffic stays in the same Availability Zone using private IP addresses. There will be data transfer charges between your NAT gateway and EC2 instance if they are in a different Availability Zone.
reason: Re-derived from the Amazon VPC pricing page, NAT Gateway pricing example.

answer: The internet gateway logically provides one-to-one NAT for the instance: outbound traffic gets the instance's public IPv4 or Elastic IP address as the reply address instead of its private address, and inbound traffic to the public or Elastic IP address has its destination translated to the instance's private IPv4 address.
quote: The internet gateway logically provides the one-to-one NAT on behalf of your instance, so that when traffic leaves your VPC subnet and goes to the internet, the reply address field is set to the public IPv4 address or Elastic IP address of your instance, and not its private IP address.
reason: Re-derived from the VPC internet gateway page, 'IP addresses and NAT'; the next sentence describes the inbound translation.

answer: Regional. An Elastic IP address is for use in a specific Region only and cannot be moved to another Region; for global static IP addresses use AWS Global Accelerator.
quote: Elastic IP addresses are regional.
reason: Re-derived from the VPC Elastic IP concepts page; the EC2 guide also says 'An Elastic IP address is for use in a specific Region only, and cannot be moved to a different Region.'
